observed_events.description: The wearer picks up a separate component with a metal cylindrical body and a black shaft (a small DC motor), brings it to the transparent battery holder that already carries the green ON/OFF S1 switch, snaps it on beside that switch and sets the assembly on the clear base. The red propeller lies loose on the table.

The wearer picks up a green PRESS switch component and the red elongated lamp component, lays them in front of the base and joins them with blue connector pieces, while the motor stays snapped on the holder assembly at the top of the base.

visual_review.scope_limit: The bounded interval was reviewed through all ordered 0.5-second samples, three native-resolution keyframes and the eight released frames. This is not a claim of uninterrupted native-rate playback or whole-recording review.

screening_lineage.discovery_method: Manual review of an EgoOops event previously screened only as a shopping-compatibility hypothesis.

prior_review.finding: The switch-retention event was visually viable, but exact spare-part compatibility prevented the shopping formulation from closing.

screening_lineage.repair: The same physical decision is mapped to saving a public wiring tutorial. This removes unsupported exact-part compatibility without changing the observed target or retain mechanism.

instruction_freeze.rule: Keep the request and both observation-conditioned queries unchanged while reviewing the complete result windows; reject mismatching videos rather than add hidden voltage, brand or connector requirements.

supported_claims.text: In the initial packet the wearer holds a component with a metal cylindrical body and black shaft beside the transparent battery holder that already carries the green ON/OFF S1 switch, then snaps it on beside that switch.
By the end of the initial packet the motor component sits on the holder assembly next to the S1 switch on the clear base.
The later packet shows a green PRESS switch and a red lamp component being joined with blue connectors in front of the base while the motor stays on the holder assembly.
Neither later component replaces the motor or changes the unchanged request about the part snapped on beside the switch.
